verdict.rationale: Glama documents per-tool access control to enable or disable individual tools on hosted servers. Its Gateway claims every MCP call is access-controlled and that 'you decide what it's allowed to do', which covers the per-tool half of the story. The evidence never describes server-level allowlisting, policy configuration, or per-agent scoping, and all support is vendor marketing copy. Missing for 10: a documented server-level allowlist of which servers an agent may call, details of how access policies are defined and scoped per agent or key, per-tool control beyond Glama-hosted servers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can restrict which servers and individual tools an agent may call through allowlists or per-tool access control

citations.quote: Per-tool access control – enable or disable individual tools
